title: Multiplexed stream auth: preserve signed signatures across reconnects and evolve preflight nonce headers
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent auth failures for multiplexed streaming clients (browser SDK using SSE/WS multiplexing and server-side HTTP/2 multiplexers) during reconnects and when edge proxies split preflight and streaming connections. Root causes: (1) ephemeral per-connection signed headers (X-Redwood-Signed, X-Redwood-Nonce) were not reliably propagated across reconnection flows and multiplexed substreams, and (2) CORS preflight behavior on some enterprise proxies stripped or rewrote nonce-prefetch headers used by the OpenAI-compat layer. This PR stabilizes the auth surface by: - Introducing persist-signed-session middleware that binds a short-lived signature token to a reconnectable session-id (X-Redwood-Session) and ensures the runtime accepts either the original per-request signed header or the session-bound token during a reconnect window. - Splitting the preflight nonce semantics into two headers: X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce (for preflight/signed-session bootstrap) and X-Redwood-Stream-Nonce (for in-band stream frames). This makes proxies less likely to remove the bootstrap header while preserving in-stream integrity checks. - Adding compatibility shim for OpenAI-compat streaming where existing clients send Authorization: Bearer project:... or org:... tokens; the shim will translate project-scoped bearer tokens into session-bound signatures when the request indicates a long-lived streaming intent (stream=true or transports: ["sse","ws"]). - Ensuring function/tool-calling metadata (toolcall-signer headers and prefetched function manifests) are replay-safe across reconnects by including a checksum header X-Redwood-Toolcall-Checksum and validating it on reconnect. Key implementation details: - runtime/server: new middleware in runtime/auth/session_store.go that issues and validates session tokens and enforces a configurable reconnect_window_ms (default 15000ms). - streaming layer: changes in streaming/stream_muxer.go to attach session-id to substreams and to accept either per-request signature or session token on reconnect. - http proxy adapter: change in adapters/proxy_cors.go to preserve X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce across preflight responses and to echo a small probe header (X-Redwood-Proxy-Probe) used by client-side checks. - openai-compat: compat/openai_stream_bridge.go updated to detect project-scoped bearer tokens and issue a temporary session token pair. - tests: new e2e for reconnect behavior (tests/e2e/stream_reconnect_auth_test.go), and unit tests for nonce-splitting logic. Checklist: - [x] Add session-store and token lifecycle (runtime + tests) - [x] Update streaming muxer and client probes - [x] Implement header split and proxy adapter changes - [x] Add openai-compat shim and docs note - [x] Add e2e reconnect tests that run in CI - [x] Document migration notes in docs/streaming-auth.md Migration notes and operator action: - Default behavior is backward compatible: existing per-request signatures continue to work. The new session-id flow is additive and opt-in via client flags or when the client sends a streaming intent field. - Operators who deploy custom proxies should ensure adapters/proxy_cors.go changes are applied or that their proxies are configured to forward X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce and not strip small unrecognized headers. Rollback plan: revert the feature flag for session-bound tokens (feature.session_auth=false) which disables the session-store acceptance and restores strict per-request signature validation. Related: ENG-4218 touches reconnect heuristics and ENG-4321 documents enterprise proxy behavior. Links: RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4218/multiplexed-stream-auth-rfc Docs: https://redwood.example/docs/streaming-auth.html

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) the reconnect window default seems long for high-rotation tokens (15s). Can we make this configurable via env and add an integration test that asserts both short and long windows?
Aisha Kapoor: Good call — made the reconnect_window_ms configurable with env REDWOOD_SESSION_RECONNECT_MS and added test vectors for 2500ms and 15000ms in tests/e2e.
Sofia Ortega: The proxy probe header is clever. Would we be able to make the probe optional? Some proxies log unknown headers. Suggest exposing it behind feature.probe_header flag.
Aisha Kapoor: Probe header is now behind feature.probe_header, default on for browsers but off for server-to-server flows. Updated docs.
Devon Park: Approving after CI pass and one minor nit about variable naming in session_store.go (sessionToken -> session_token to match style).
Aisha Kapoor: Renamed the variable and pushed fixup commit. Thanks!
merge_commit: squash: 4e7b9fa - Merge feature/stream-auth-stability: preserve signed session tokens and split nonce headers
release_notes: Stabilized streaming auth for multiplexed connections: session-bound signatures and split preflight/stream nonces. Backward compatible; operators may need to ensure proxies forward X-Redwood-Prefetch-Nonce. See docs/streaming-auth.md for migration steps.
notes: This PR was merged after a short staged rollout to Dedicated clusters and monitoring for parity metrics (auth_failure_rate, stream_reconnect_latency). Observed a 78% reduction in auth failures during reconnects in canary.
